predecessors.name: Chola Empire
predecessors.text: Kalinga, which 'the Cholas brought ... under their rule' in the 11th century

successors.name: Suryavamsha Dynasty
successors.text: the Ganga realm: 'his minister Kapilendra usurped the throne and founded the Suryavamsha dynasty in 1434-35'

ledger.x: 1078: Anantavarman Chodaganga becomes king and the Ganga empire begins.
1078: the Cholas take the Visakhapatnam district.

c. 1102: the Cholas take Kalinga proper in Kulottunga's second Kalinga war. 'The first war seems to have occurred before 1096'; 'The second invasion took place a few years later, sometime before the 33rd year of the king's reign', led by his general Karunakara Tondaiman, who 'defeated the Kalinga ruler Anantavarman…
1118: Utkala is Ganga.

c. 1118 (bridge): Chodaganga recovers the Visakhapatnam district. 'for a while Chodaganga lost to them a part of his kingdom comprising the Visakhapatnam district but he did not lose heart and gradually recovered his lost territories' (Eastern Ganga page, no year). The Chodaganga page has his 'empire extended to river…

c. 1118-1122 (bridge): Chodaganga takes the north of Vengi. 'It seems that Chodaganga saw this as an advantage and conquered the part of Vengi lying north to river Godavari', where 'this' is the Chola weakness at Kulottunga's death, which the Chodaganga page dates to 1118 ('After the death of Kulottunga in 1118 AD…

c. 1126 (bridge): Kalinga proper is Ganga again. No page dates the recovery from the Cholas; the Chodaganga page has an empire from the Ganga to the Godavari at his death in 1150 and the Kulottunga page has the northern half of Vengi 'seems to have slipped' from Chola hands late in the reign; Cliopatria shrinks the…

c. 1150 (bridge): Kamarnava VII fights for Sambalpur. 'During his reign he fought with the Kalachuris of Ratnapura for the possession of the Sambalpur- Bolangir Tract but was unsuccessful' (ruler list c. 1150-1156). The page gives no year and no battle, so his reign is used (confidence 1). No land changes hands. This…

1152: Cliopatria's shape loses 104 cells; 15 of them lie in the Visakhapatnam district (by the gazetteer test), which the dossier keeps from its recovery in 1118, leaving 89 cells in the south-west of the old shape.
1152 (bridge): the Vengi strip leaves the shape.
c. 1156 (bridge): the fight ends in failure at the end of Kamarnava VII's reign ('but was unsuccessful'). The tract stays with the Kalachuris of Ratnapura until Anangabhima III's conquest (1211).
1211 (earliest year of the reign; bridge): Anangabhima III takes the Sambalpur tract.
1243: Narasimha I's army moves on Bengal.
1244: Odia forces occupy Rarh and Gauda.
1247: Delhi sends a new governor.
1247 (bridge): the occupation of Rarh and Gauda is taken to end.

c. 1260 (bridge): Cliopatria adds 238 cells (17 of them the Visakhapatnam district, already Ganga since 1118, so the gain is 221) (Chhattisgarh 83, Jharkhand 30, Odisha 84, Andhra Pradesh 41, Visakhapatnam side 41). Narasimha I 'followed the policy of aggressive imperialism' until 1264 and 'humbled the Kakatiya king…
1353: Firuz Shah Tughlaq invades Odisha.
1358: the Tughlaq invasion ends.
1358: the Ganga king pays tribute to Delhi.
1359 (bridge): the tint ends.
1434: Kapilendra ends the Eastern Gangas.

wars.name: Ganga-Chola wars over Kalinga and Vengi
wars.outcome: The Cholas take the Visakhapatnam district early in Chodaganga's reign ('gradually recovered', c.

wars.name: Ganga-Kalachuri conflict for Kosala and Sambalpur
wars.outcome: A 'long conflict for the control of the Trikalinga and Kosala regions': Ratnadeva II (1120-1135) 'repulsed an invasion by Anantavarman Chodaganga'; Kamarnava VII fought for the Sambalpur-Bolangir Tract 'but was unsuccessful'; Anangabhima III 'conquered the…

wars.name: Khalji attack on Jajnagar
wars.outcome: 'In 1205 Bakhtiyar Khalji sent Muhammad Sheran Khalji with a portion of his forces towards Jajnagar'; 'the first invasion of Muslims in Odisha was unsuccessful'.

wars.name: Narasimha I's Bengal campaign
wars.outcome: The Odia army seizes Rarh and Varendra in 1244, besieges Lakhnauti, is counter-attacked by Tughril Tughan Khan near Katasin (Contai) and is pushed back after Yuzbak's appointment in 1247; Rarh and Gauda 'stayed under Odia control' according to the page while…

wars.name: Firuz Shah Tughlaq's invasion of Odisha
wars.outcome: Tribute was levied on the Ganga king; no territorial result is on the page.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on any page; Bengal and Vengi frontiers were fought over each decade and the interior is given only as district names.
